unit#1 was traveling nb in the 1300 block of sh 75 north. as unit#1 traveled nb, it struck the pedestrian, when it's driver did not see him standing in the roadway. the pedestrain died at the scene from injuries he sustained. robert navarro is the driver of the listed truck tractor and attached trailer. during my scene investigation, he advised me that his attached trailer was to the center line of the roadway when the pedestrian was struck. due to this reported accident being fatal. see attached supplement reports for additional report information. supplement:on this date, police responded to the scene at the request of cpl. galle. i was briefed about the scene. i marked the scene and took photographs of the scene. i spoke to the driver of unit #2. he advised that he was attempting to back his attached trailer(unit#3) onto 75 [roadway]. the deceased stood in the roadway to assist the driver of unit#2 in backing up. the driver of unit#2 further advised that the rear of his trailer was about to the center line when the crash occurred. i then spoke to the driver of unit#1 who advised that he never saw the deceased, that he only felt the collision. though my investigation, it was determined that due to time of day and limited visibility, the driver of unit#1, never saw the [roadway]. after the collision, the deceased was carried by unit#1, then fell off and was ran over by unit #1. the deceased [roadway] [roadway] 75 north. supplement by sgt. m. legerski, 211. on [date], i received a call from corporal hurst, who requested that i respond to assist him at a fatality accident. i responded from my residence and arrived at 0741 hours. upon arrival, i met with corporal hurst and gallee and was briefed on what had occurred. i observed the 18-wheeler truck pulled into the private parking lotof omar's automotive, located at [roadway] of traffic, and the shoe was facing southwest towards the rear of the 18-wheeler box. north of the left shoe, 65. 10 feet, lay the right shoe. it was facing se. there was a small amount of blood (spot 1) and tissue on the asphalt 6. 7 ft north of the right shoe. this is evidence of where the body came off the hood of the car and struck the ground. twenty-eight feet north of spot 1 wasanother blood spot, spot 2. from spottwo, the ground was disturbed as if swept as the body was being pushed in front of and/or dragged under the car 34. 45 ft to the center mass/belt line. from the right shoe to the left rear tire of the car was 71. 8 feet. the body was already gone by the time i arrived, but the blood was still present, and hurst had painted the head and feet areas on the ground. a white dodge challenger with black racing stripes over the hood was parked, still idling, [roadway] of traffic. the car's grill, hood, windshield, and cab were damaged. the windshield was completely breached, and there was some brain matter towards the top of the windshield where the cab meets it. there were no skid marks. faint tracks in the loose gravel werevisible on [roadway], indicating that the rightside of the car traveled through it,but definitely did not lock up and skid, only rolled to a controlled stop. the left, driver side, tires remained on the roadway asphalt, which was very freshly laid. i did not utilize the drag sled toobtain a coefficient of friction, asit would not be neededfor any speed calculations on this scene. hurst had already marked the scene with paint. i had him take some measurements of the car's hood, windshield, and cab. we then measured the scene with a mechanical roller, and i called out trent sanders to fly the scene with the drone. i assisted with traffic control until the drone flight was complete. snaggs wrecker was on scene, and i told him he could hook up, and he did so.. i made note that the lights were still on on the challenger, and it was still running. the wrecker driver reached in and pushed the ignition kill switch and turned the vehicle off. he then hooked up and lifted the car up as far as he could, and hurst and i looked underneath the car to see if there was any tissue or blood. i did not see any conclusive evidence that the car had completely run over the pedestrian. while we were still on the scene waiting for officer sanders to fly the scene and photograph it with the drone, a car pulled into the business. hurst and i made contact with the driver, who was the co-owner of the business. with his assistance, we were able to put cid in touch with the deceased's wife. i left the scene and went back to my regular duties. based on the circumstances of the accident and the evidence at the scene, i do not believe the car was travelling in excess of the speed limit, which is 60 mph. it appeared that the pedestrian was not wearing any reflective clothing and was likely very hard to see. the pedestrian was failing to yield row to the traffic on sh 75 and did not see or hear the car for whatever reason. as stated earlier, its lights were still on. on [date], i returned to the scene and remeasured, starting from the first left shoe and working north to the body and then to the car. i also looked for the victim's phone and wallet in the grass and did not find either. end of supplement.

records.deidentified_narrative: on september 9, 2025 at approximately 2040hrs i, officer e. rodriguez #5164 and officer estrada #4802 were dispatched to a major accident. upon arriving at 2047hrs we noticed our victim to be laying on the ground. the victim was getting medical attention when we arrived. we tried to ask the victim what happened, but she kept yelling due to the pain she was having. the victim was finally able to give her name to officers. when she was asked about what happened the victim stated she did not know and also mentioned she was not sure if she was hit by a vehicle. the victim's friend stated he did not see a vehicle, but heard the ""thump"" and then heard something metal being dragged. there were also no witnesses that saw what happened. the victim was just found laying on the roadway. her friend moved her out of the roadway to the curbside until helped arrived. the victim had abrasions to her legs, arms and stomach. the rtcc(real time crime center) was able to see a vehicle with no headlights traveling westbound, but unable to give us any other descriptors . the victim was unable to give us details of what actually occurred to her. i provided the victim with a report number and advised her to call us if she remembers anything that happened.
